q: All of the following cause chronic diarrhoea EXCEPT:
A 2-year-old has loose stools with undigested vegetables 4 times a day for months; he drinks much juice and grows normally. The diagnosis is:
e: Chronic non-specific (toddler's) diarrhoea: normal growth, undigested food, excess juice.

q: The best screening test for coeliac disease is:
e: tTG-IgA is the best test; total IgA excludes IgA deficiency.

q: Regarding coeliac disease, all are true EXCEPT:
o: It is a T-cell reaction to gluten
Treatment is a lifelong gluten-free diet
It may present with short stature
It is linked with Down syndrome
e: Rice and maize are gluten-free and safe.

q: Biopsy findings of coeliac disease include all EXCEPT:
A teenager has weight loss, short stature, abdominal pain and a perianal fistula. The most likely diagnosis is:
e: Perianal disease, growth failure and transmural fistulae are typical of Crohn disease.

q: Frothy acidic stools with sore buttocks after rotavirus gastroenteritis are best managed by:
o: Continue breastfeeding; lactose-free formula if formula-fed
e: Secondary lactose intolerance is temporary; continue breastfeeding.

q: A 13-month-old has chronic diarrhoea since 3 months of age, failure to thrive and stools positive for reducing sugars with no pathogens. The most likely diagnosis is:
e: Onset at 3 months on milk with damaged mucosa fits cow's milk protein enteropathy; coeliac needs wheat after 6 months.

q: The formula of choice for a formula-fed infant with cow's milk protein allergy is:
e: Lactose-free formula still contains cow's milk protein.

q: IMCI management of persistent diarrhoea with some dehydration is:
e: Severe persistent diarrhoea (any dehydration) is referred.
